triples.relationship: Reward parallel: a crown for those who endure
triples.rationale: Zechariah says the crown will be for those who endure, among the other native descriptions of its recipients and use. James calls the person enduring trial blessed and promises the approved person the crown of life. Both explicitly join endurance with receiving a crown. James' crown of life is not identified with the silver-and-gold crown of Zechariah's context, and it does not resolve Zephaniah's son or the other listed descriptions.
triples.source_text: The crown will be for those who endure, for its useful people and those who have known it, for the favor of Zephaniah’s son and for a psalm in the Lord’s house.

target_units.text: Blessed is the man who endures a trial, because, having been approved, he will receive the crown of life that He promised to those who love Him.

triples.rationale: Zechariah promises the gathered prisoners settlement in a stronghold and double repayment in exchange for a day of sojourn. Job says that the Lord gave him double what he formerly possessed, after his prayer for his friends. Both state a divine doubling as a benefit following prior adversity. Job does not supply a one-day equivalence or a prison-to-stronghold setting, and the two recipients and measures of restoration remain distinct.
triples.source_text: You will settle in a stronghold, prisoners of the gathering; in exchange for one day of your sojourn I will repay you double.

target_units.text: The Lord increased Job. When he also prayed for his friends, He forgave their sin. The Lord gave double what Job had formerly, for a doubling.

triples.relationship: Community ethic: received benefit prevents boasting over others
triples.rationale: Zechariah says the Lord saves Judah's dwellings so that David's house and Jerusalem will not exalt themselves over Judah. Paul likewise warns against being puffed up in favor of one against another and challenges boasting as if received gifts were not received. Both oppose one part of a community magnifying itself over another on the basis of what it has been given. Paul's community and its teachers are not identified with Judah, Jerusalem or David's house.
triples.source_text: The Lord will save Judah’s dwellings as from the beginning, so that the boasting of David’s house and Jerusalem’s residents’ exaltation will not magnify itself over Judah.

target_units.text: Now, brothers, I have applied these things figuratively to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that in us you may learn, “Not beyond what is written,” so that none of you may be puffed up in favor of one against another.
For who makes you different? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?

triples.relationship: Lament imagery: lost pomegranate growth and communal grief
triples.rationale: Zechariah compares Jerusalem's great mourning with mourning for a pomegranate grove cut down in a plain. Joel calls for mourning because the plains and crops have suffered, specifically includes dried-up pomegranate trees, and commands the ministers to lament. Both connect communal mourning with the loss of pomegranate growth in the land. Joel's drying is not equated with cutting down, and Zechariah's grove is not turned into an alternate place name or a named battle.
triples.source_text: On that day mourning in Jerusalem will grow great, like mourning over a pomegranate grove cut down in a plain,

target_units.text: because the plains have suffered. Let the earth mourn, because grain has suffered, wine has dried up, and oil has diminished.
The farmers have dried up. Lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest from the field has perished.
The vine has dried up and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate, palm, apple tree and all the field’s trees have dried up, because human beings have put joy to shame.

Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.
